assumptions: The service is positioned as readiness and evidence assembly rather than regulated or certified assurance.
Qualified cybersecurity specialists can be contracted at costs consistent with the stated contribution-margin range.
The founder maintains strict separation from employer resources and can allocate approximately 15 hours weekly.
evidence_needed_for_higher_score: Several paid sprints from clearly in-scope Polish organizations, measured delivery hours and contribution margins, repeatable partner referrals, refresh renewals, and counsel-confirmed assurance boundaries.

factors.name: Core insight
factors.rationale: Regulatory obligations create a real evidence-assembly bottleneck, and separating orchestration from specialist assurance is a sensible productization insight.

factors.name: Customer pain and willingness to pay
factors.rationale: Audits, board requests, questionnaires, and incidents create funded urgency, although Polish scope, budgets, and paid conversion remain unverified.

factors.name: Business model and economics
factors.rationale: Upfront fixed-price work supports cash conversion and refreshes could recur, but assumed margins, partner splits, sales cycles, and the 180-sprint scale case are unproven.

factors.name: Market and beachhead
factors.rationale: Mid-market Polish entities facing NIS2 or supply-chain pressure form a coherent beachhead, but the realistically addressable in-scope population is unknown.

factors.name: Competitive position and domination potential
factors.rationale: Rapid, standardized delivery could win a niche, but consultancies and MSPs can reproduce the offer and presently control trust and specialist capacity.

factors.name: Expansion potential
factors.rationale: Recurring control refreshes, adjacent standards, supplier assurance, and broader EU markets provide credible extensions after establishing delivery credibility.

factors.name: Defensibility and durability
factors.rationale: Permissioned mappings and benchmarks could compound, but evidence remains client-owned and the workflow is readily copied without embedded integrations or proprietary data scale.

factors.name: Strength of advantage
factors.rationale: A fixed-duration, board-ready deliverable can be faster and clearer than open-ended consulting, though the magnitude of improvement is not demonstrated.

factors.name: Timing and momentum
factors.rationale: Active regulatory implementation and supply-chain scrutiny create a strong near-term purchasing window despite national variation.

factors.name: Distribution
factors.rationale: MSP and audit-firm referrals are plausible and founder-compatible, but no referral agreement, customer relationship, or acquisition performance exists.

factors.name: Execution and risks
factors.rationale: The capital and part-time orchestration fit, but credential gaps, evidence security, professional liability, and dependence on qualified specialists are material.

highest_value_structural_change: Secure a qualified cyber-firm channel partnership with standardized scope, liability allocation, referral economics, and recurring evidence-refresh rights.
main_structural_strength: A high-ticket, urgent compliance workflow can be productized and sold with favorable upfront cash collection.
primary_score_limiter: The offer lacks controlled distribution, specialist capacity, and a durable advantage over established cybersecurity consultancies.
strongest_disconfirming_evidence: The founder has no stated cybersecurity credentials or contracted specialist capacity, while incumbents can offer substantially similar assessments.
